{{Quote|An army of one man, but the right man for the job.|[[Clone trooper/Legends|Clone trooper]] rallying call|<ref name="LOE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref>}}
The '''Grand Army of the Republic''' ('''GAR'''), also known as the '''Grand Army''', '''Clone Army''', '''Army of the Republic''' or '''Republic Army''', was a major branch of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Republic Military/Legends|Military]] composed entirely of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], an [[Army/Legends|army]] of elite [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] [[Cloning/Legends|created]] from the [[DNA/Legends|genetically]] altered [[Clone template/Legends|template]] of the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]. Bred in secret within the [[Tipoca City/Legends|cloning facilities]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], the Grand Army was officially formed by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] at the behest of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] in response to the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] which threatened to divide [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] between the Republic and the newly born [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. The members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] were commissioned as high-ranking [[Jedi Commander/Legends|commanders]] and [[Jedi General/Legends|generals]] in the GAR, second in authority only to Chancellor Palpatine, who held the rank of [[Supreme Commander (Republic)|Supreme Commander]]. Under the leadership of their [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] officers, the Grand Army engaged the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] on many worlds during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], suffering heavy casualties for three years while restoring Republic sovereignty to numerous rebellious areas throughout the galaxy.

By the year [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Clone Wars were nearly over and the Republic was on the verge of a decisive victory. In the midst of the final battles, particularly in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Campaign]], Chancellor Palpatine issued [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]], an [[Contingency Orders for the Grand Army of the Republic: Order Initiation, Orders 1 Through 150|executive command]] calling on all clone [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] to neutralize their Jedi officers with [[Death/Legends|lethal force]] in the event of a [[Showdown on Coruscant|Jedi insurrection]]. The vast majority of clones, [[Inhibitor chip/Legends|genetically engineered for loyalty and conditioned to obey all orders without question or debate]], turned their weapons on the Jedi and promptly gunned them down. On [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the newly-anointed [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] led the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] in an [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|attack]] on the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], [[Death/Legends|killing]] nearly all of its inhabitants within mere days before the Chancellor's [[Declaration of a New Order]]. Immediately following the Republic's transition into the first [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Grand Army of the Republic was reorganized into the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]]; its remaining clone [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] composing the ranks of the reformed branch in addition to the millions of [[Clone stormtrooper|new clones]] engineered by [[Spaarti cloning cylinder|Spaarti technology]]. Under the reign of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine, the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Imperial stormtroopers]] became a symbol of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], most notably due to their unwavering loyalty to the Emperor. Likewise, what's left of the Grand Army of the Republic formed the basis of the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]], which acted as the surface warfare branch of the Imperial Military, with the human commanders being promoted to being the officers within the branch.

At the end of the Clone Wars, it was discovered that Palpatine was secretly [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Sidious, a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] who belonged to an [[Order of the Sith Lords|order]] dedicated to the fall of the Republic and the destruction of the Jedi. As Palpatine and Sidious, the Dark Lord controlled both sides of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|civil war]], deceived both the Jedi and Confederacy, and used the GAR as an instrument to restore [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] rule to the galaxy while simultaneously [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|purging]] it of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]. As a result, the GAR was remembered as a key factor in the [[Grand Plan/Legends|Sith plot]] that brought about the [[Imperial Era/Legends|era of the Dark Times]] and the subsequent [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].

==History==
{{Quote|As my first act with this new authority, I will create a Grand Army of the Republic to counter the increasing threats of the Separatists.|Supreme Chancellor Palpatine|<ref name="AOTC" />}}
[[File:Clone_Army_patch.svg|thumb|left|115px|A [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] patch that signified involvement in the secret Republic [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] project.]]
At the beginning of the [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] administration ([[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]), the Republic had no standing armed forces, though the debate about the reinstatement of an army and [[Republic Navy/Legends|navy]] had been ongoing for decades. The only military forces were the Jedi, which kept peace for generations. The Jedi were no army though. At one time, the Republic's military forces were considerable, but in the wake of the [[New Sith Wars]] ([[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]), a gradual process of down scaling began, in favor of increased support from the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="DB:ROT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>

More and more often, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were called upon to act as negotiators. But as crises piled upon each other, some within the Order began to sense a coming darkness, which their numbers alone would not be sufficient to fight. The creation of a clone army was secretly ordered by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Sifo-Dyas]] without the knowledge or approval of his comrades, in response to the growing shadow in the Force.<ref name="LOE" /> Sifo-Dyas had been manipulated into placing the order by Sith Lord [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], in his guise as Hego Damask, who used his own wealth and that of the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|Banking Clan]] to fund the army. Plagueis believed the Kaminoans would only accept the order if it came from a Jedi due to the Kaminoans' interest in them.<ref name="Star Wars: Darth Plagueis" />

Not too long after Plagueis was betrayed and murdered by his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], who became the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], Sidious had his apprentice [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]], the latter being the former Jedi Master Count Dooku, betray and orchestrate the death of Sifo-Dyas, and the two then took over the project. Sifo-Dyas had an [[Inhibitor chip/Legends|inhibitor chip]] he wanted instilled in each Clone, which was to be a safeguard against rogue Jedi's. However, Tyranus and Sidious retooled the chips to brainwash the Clones into murdering the Jedi, in order for the [[Grand Plan/Legends|Sith to reclaim control of the galaxy]]. Posing as a Jedi, Tyranus presented the Kaminoans the chip and tricked them into believing Sifo-Dyas's intention.

The GAR's first engagement would be at the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]],<ref name="AOTC" /> where it successfully routed an unsuspecting droid army. However, this merely started off the much larger [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], in which the army took heavy losses.

However, some Jedi such as [[Bardan Jusik]] felt that the Jedi Order was actually using it as a slave army, since the clones were not allowed any leave or rest, and had to fight continuously. This eventually led to Jusik leaving the Jedi Order, disgusted by its actions in allowing the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] to use an army in such a manner.

Though the clone troopers fought under the Jedi for most of the Clone Wars, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] Palpatine, secretly Darth Sidious, [[Security Act amendment|wrested]] executive control over the army from the Jedi late in the war<ref name="ROTSn">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> by issuing [[Order 66]], which led to the inhibitor chips brainwashing the Clones into destroying the Jedi Order, and thus beginning the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]]. Palpatine created the Galactic Empire on the eve of the war's end.<ref name="ROTS" /> Having declared himself [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], Palpatine quickly transformed the clone army into the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]] and integrated it into the military of his new Empire.

After [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] and the Jedi Purge, a number of clones deserted the Grand Army. Most of these clones were from the [[Special Operations Brigade/Legends|Special Operations Brigade]], including the partial [[Omega Squad]], [[Null-class Advanced Recon Commando]] and some [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|Advanced Recon Commandos]] such as Captain [[Maze (clone trooper)|Maze]].

Before the end of the war, the [[Sector Governance Decree/Legends|Sector Governance Decree]] was issued, which placed governors on every world of the Republic, along with their own force of clone troopers. It also created the position of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] or sector governor. Fearing for the future of democracy and the Senate's powers, this decision was one of several protested by the [[Delegation of 2000]], but they were overruled.<ref name="ROTSn" /> Governors and their clone regiments began arriving on their designated worlds soon after.<ref name="ROTSVD">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

The total amount of clones involved in the war is not known, as their ranks were bolstered by new stocks and volunteers as the fighting dragged on. With the formation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the Grand Army of the Republic ceased to exist and was reorganized into the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. All military personnel of the GAR were required to swear allegiance to the new government in order to remain on active duty and those that refused were branded as deserters and traitors after which they were hunted down and executed.<ref name="CNI:JT">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref>

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], clones of Jango Fett's lineage made up about 1/3 of all stormtroopers in the Galactic Empire, but it is not known how many were left from the Clone Wars by the start of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="SWI96">[[Star Wars Insider 96|''Star Wars Insider'' 96]]</ref> Due to the influx of non-Fett clones and regular humans into the army, the Fett clones, such as [[Cody/Legends|Commander Cody]], viewed the Stormtrooper Corps as an embarrassment to the legacy of the Grand Army of the Republic.

==Organization==
===Headquarters===
{{Quote|In response, the Old Republic assembled its own army by leveraging mysterious cloning technology to create a near-limitless supply of troops.|Description of the Republic building up its military|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Grand_army_formation.jpg|thumb|right|230px|[[Clone trooper/Legends|Clone troopers]] fall in formation for deployment.]]
The GAR and the entire [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] were constitutionally re-established after the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] granted Supreme Chancellor Palpatine emergency powers during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], giving him the right to create a Republic army.<ref name="AOTC" /> The GAR was thus ultimately led by the [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]], who held the military titles of [[Supreme Commander (Republic)|Supreme Commander]] and [[Commander-in-Chief/Legends|Commander-in-Chief]]. The GAR and the rest of the Republic Military was administered through the [[Department of Defense]].<ref name="Order66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> Other executive bodies with authority over the Grand Army included the [[War Council Advisory Panel/Legends|War Council Advisory Panel]].<ref name="ROTSVD" />

Legislative oversight of the GAR was provided by the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate's]] [[Military Oversight Committee/Legends|Military Oversight Committee]].<ref name="The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The senior military body in command of the Grand Army and the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] was [[Republic High Command/Legends|Republic High Command]],<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> led by the [[Chief of Defense Staff]].<ref name="Order66" /> [[GAR Headquarters]]—the central command for the Grand Army—was based at [[Coruscant Command HQ]],<ref name="RC:TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> near the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]].<ref name="HQ note">The ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' novel establishes the location of [[GAR Headquarters]] to be near the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. As ''Republic Commando: Triple Zero'' places the Headquarters at [[Coruscant Command HQ]], it could be found that the latter structure was also near the Jedi Temple on Coruscant.</ref>

===Administration===
Command HQ maintained a number of branches to administrate the Grand Army. One of these was the [[Republic Defense Procurement Office/Legends|Republic Defense Procurement office]], which was in permanent contact with the GAR's field [[logistics battalion]]s.<ref name="RC:TZ" /> Research and development into new technologies was carried out by the [[Army Weapons Research Department]].

One particularly visible branch of the GAR was [[Homeworld Security Command]], responsible for the security of the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Homeworld Security controlled the [[Coruscant Guard/Legends|Coruscant Guard]], whose distinctive, red-armored [[Clone shock trooper/Legends|clone shock troopers]] had broad discretionary powers to stop and search Republic citizens.<ref name="LOE" /> When the [[Declaration of a New Order]] established the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], clone shock troopers were stationed in the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building]] and [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]] to intimidate the Senate into ensuring a smooth transition of government.<ref name="ROTSn" />

A number of GAR facilities were constructed by [[Kaminoan droid]]s, especially during the [[Decimator (war machine)|Decimator]] [[Hunt for the Decimator|campaign]].<ref name="GTTGAOTR">{{InsiderCite|84|Guide to the Grand Army of the Republic}}</ref>

===Tactical organization===
The army was split into separate [[Order of Battle/Legends|Orders of Battle]] (ORBATs). These were regular forces and special forces. Most of the structure of the regular forces was unchanged through the Clone Wars and was even used by the Galactic Empire. The special forces were highly independent [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] that had specific objectives and required very little help from Jedi commanders.<ref name="GTTGAOTR" />

====Command structure of regular forces====
{{Quote|…if the GAR were made up of average humans, you simply would not have a functioning army now. Clone troopers are optimized humans, and only two percent of the population could be as tough, resilient and aggressive as these men are.|[[Mij Gilamar]], on reports that clone troopers do not feel pain, because they were created for war, and bred for it|<ref name="Order66" />}}
*'''Grand Army'''—10 systems armies (3,000,000 troopers) led by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="GTTGAOTR" /> The number 3,000,000 was Sifo-Dyas' initial order, as the number of total clones increased during the war.<ref name="EGW" />
*'''[[Systems Army/Legends|Systems Army]]'''—2 Sector Armies (294,912 troopers) led by a [[High Jedi General/Legends|High Jedi General]] (Jedi High Council Member).<ref name="GTTGAOTR" /><ref name="EGW" />
*'''[[Sector Army/Legends|Sector Army]]'''—4 corps (147,456 troopers) led by a [[Senior Jedi General]] (Jedi Master).<ref name="GTTGAOTR" /><ref name="EGW" />
*'''[[Corps/Legends|Corps]]/Division'''—4 legions (36,864 troopers) led by a [[Clone Marshal Commander/Legends|Marshal Commander]] and a [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] (Jedi Knight or Master).<ref name="GTTGAOTR" /><ref name="EGW" />
*'''[[Legion/Legends|Legion]]/[[Brigade/Legends|Brigade]]'''—4 regiments (9,216 troopers) led by a [[Senior clone commander|Senior Commander]] and a Jedi General (Jedi Knight).<ref name="GTTGAOTR" /><ref name="EGW" />
*'''[[Regiment/Legends|Regiment]]'''—4 battalions (2,304 troopers) led by a [[Clone regimental commander|Regimental Commander]] and a [[Jedi Commander/Legends|Jedi Commander]] (Jedi Padawan).<ref name="EGW" />
*'''[[Battalion/Legends|Battalion]]'''—4 companies (576 troopers) led by a [[Clone battalion commander|Battalion Commander]] and a [[Clone major/Legends|Major]].
*'''[[Company/Legends|Company]]'''—4 platoons (144 troopers) led by a [[Clone Captain/Legends|Captain and a Lieutenant]].<ref name="GTTGAOTR" /><ref name="EGW" />
*'''[[Platoon/Legends|Platoon]]'''—4 squads (36 troopers) led by a Second [[Clone Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] and Sergeant-Major.<ref name="EGW" />
*'''[[Squad/Legends|Squad]]'''—9 troopers led by a [[Clone Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] and [[Corporal/Legends|Corporal]].<ref name="EGW" />

The rate of casualties greatly reduced the Grand Army's numbers throughout the Clone Wars. Prior to the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]], many of the original Kamino clone troopers were dead or unable to continue fighting.<ref name="Order66" /> However, the [[Republic military enhancement bill/Legends|Republic military enhancement bill]]—passed by a majority vote in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] midway through the war—authorized the funding of five million additional clone troopers.<ref name="SM">{{TCW|Senate Murders}}</ref> During the waning days of the Clone Wars, millions of [[Spaarti cloning cylinder|Spaarti-grown]] clones were deployed to supplement their Kaminoan-created counterparts in the fight against the still numerically superior Separatist Army.<ref name="Order66" />

====Command structure of special forces====
*'''[[Special Operations Brigade/Legends|Special Operations Brigade]]''' ('''SO BDE''')—20 groups (10,000 troopers), commanded by [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Arligan Zey]], made up of 10 Commando Groups by one year after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]].<ref name="GTTGAOTR" />
*'''[[Commando Group]]'''—5 companies (500 troopers), the equivalent of a regular army battalion.<ref name="GTTGAOTR" />
*'''[[Company/Legends|Company]]'''—5 troops (100 troopers) led by a [[Commander/Legends|commander]].<ref name="Clone Wars Campaign Guide">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>
*'''[[Troop/Legends|Troop]]'''—5 squads (20 troopers).<ref name="GTTGAOTR" />
*'''[[Squad/Legends|Squad]]'''—4 troopers led by a [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]].<ref name="Clone Wars Campaign Guide" />

==Vehicles==
The Grand Army employed a number of vehicles drawn from the inventory of [[Rothana Heavy Engineering/Legends|Rothana Heavy Engineering]], [[Planetary defense forces|local planetary forces]] and even captured enemy vehicles.

==='''Aerospace Vehicles'''===
While the [[Republic Starfighter Corps/Legends|Republic Starfighter Corps]] was principally part of the Republic Navy and the [[Jedi Starfighter Corps]] was part of the Jedi Order, there were a number of vehicles dedicated to support ground operations rather than merely an extension of space operations.
*[[Low Altitude Assault Transport/Legends|Low Altitude Assault Transport]]
**[[Low Altitude Assault Transport/carrier/Legends|Low Altitude Assault Transport/carrier]] — An aerial transport and towing vehicle capable of moving vehicles, building materials, and even large animals.
**[[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry]] — An atmospheric gunship capable of transporting up to 30 passengers into combat.
***[[Space gunship/Legends|Space gunship]] — A variant that could be deployed from space without its transport having to breach the stratosphere.
*[[Republic police gunship/Legends|Republic police gunship]] — A patrol and internal security airspeeder.
*[[High-Altitude Entry Transport-221/Legends|High-Altitude Entry Transport-221]] — A high altitude gunboat and reconnaissance platform.
*[[PTB-625 planetary bomber/Legends|PTB-625 planetary bomber]] — An airspeeder designed for surface bombardment.
*[[CR20 troop carrier/Legends|CR20 troop carrier]] — An interstellar troop transport capable of deploying 40 passengers under fire.

==='''Surface Vehicles'''===
*[[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|All Terrain Tactical Enforcer]] — A six-legged weapons platform and troop transport.
*[[All Terrain Experimental Transport|All Terrain Experimental Transport]] — An enclosed one-man bipedal walker.
*[[All Terrain Reconnaissance Transport|All Terrain Recon Transport]] — A light one-man bipedal walker, introduced later in the war.
*[[All Terrain Open Transport/Legends|All Terrain Open Transport]] — An eight-legged troop transport, capable of carrying at least 34 passengers in its standard configuration, but able to carry more passengers (or other cargo) in its reconfigurable open bed.
*[[All Terrain Attack Pod/Legends|All Terrain Attack Pod]] — A three-legged walker built around a powerful main cannon.
*[[Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery/Legends|Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery walker]] — A twelve-legged, slow-moving modular artillery platform.
*[[Unstable Terrain Artillery Transport/Legends|Unstable Terrain Artillery Transport]] — An armored repulsorcraft designed later in the war for use on terrain that was too unstable even for walkers.
*[[TX-130 Saber-class fighter tank/Legends|TX-130 Saber-class fighter tank]] — A fast, agile repulsortank.
*[[Republic Troop Transport/Legends|Republic Troop Transport]] — A heavily-armored repulsorcraft used to transport up to 12 passengers into dangerous areas.
*[[Infantry Support Platform/Legends|Infantry Support Platform]] — A two-man repulsorcraft, also called the "Swamp Speeder."
*[[BARC speeder/Legends|BARC Speeder]] — A fast one-man speeder bike, initially developed for use by ARC troopers, but eventually provided to the entire army.

===Suppliers===
[[BlasTech Industries/Legends|Blastech Industries]] provided large quantities of state-of-the-art weapons for the Republic, and would later provide numerous [[E-11 blaster rifle/Legends|replacements]] postwar.

The main designer and manufacturer of personal defense suits and [[Armor/Legends|body armor]] was [[Kaminoan Armorsmiths Ltd./Legends|Kaminoan Armorsmiths Ltd.]], a [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]-based company from the same planet as most of the Republic's cloned personnel.

==Personnel==
====Recruitment====
[[File:Trench_warrior_TCWCG.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Vurk warrior fights alongside clone troopers]]
Although the clones created on Kamino formed a capable fighting force for the Republic, the vast scope of the war required additional manpower from more traditional volunteers.<ref name="Galaxy at War" />

The military commanders of the time recognized that the reserves of available clones were limited, so they increased recruitment across most core and [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] worlds. Stringent recruitment quotas were set throughout the Republic's loyal systems. Human-dominated worlds were heavily targeted for recruitment, even though many of the Republic's strongest supporters come from [[Alien/Legends|non-Human]] species. Worlds and systems that failed to meet recruitment quotas were initially subjected to draft lotteries, but these eventually gave way to conscription drives, which involved the forced recruitment of able-bodied men and women.<ref name="Galaxy at War" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Grand Army of the Republic is the second "grand army" to appear in a ''Star Wars'' film, after the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] Grand Army in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']].

In the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] the terminology for Grand Army is similar to that of the [[Wikipedia:British Armed Forces|British Armed Forces]], as [[Karen Traviss]], who wrote multiple books about the GAR, is British.

===Numbers===
{{Quote|FYI, re: 3 million. LFL was very clear to us that <u>no</u> fixed number of total clones would or could be assigned. Therefore, the number 3 million (plus) does not represent the entire fighting force.|[[Ryan Kaufman (real person)|Ryan Kaufman]]|<ref name="Board">{{WebCite|url=https://boards.theforce.net/threads/guide-to-the-grand-army-insider-84.21603019/page-10#post-21642877|text=Guide to the Grand Army (Insider #84)|archivedate=20201018053645}}</ref>}}
When [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] went to Kamino in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], the Kaminoan prime minister, [[Lama Su/Legends|Lama Su]], informed him that 200,000 troops (sometimes referred to as units) were ready for deployment and a million more were on the way.

The figure of 1.2 million soldiers was accurate according to the novel [[Shatterpoint (novel)|''Shatterpoint'']] (written by [[Matthew Stover]]). Six months after the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] that amount of troops would be reached by the cloners. In ''[[Guide to the Grand Army of the Republic]]'' and the novel ''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]'' (both written by Karen Traviss, with [[Ryan Kaufman (real person)|Ryan Kaufman]] as co-author on the ''Guide…''), there were 3,000,000 clones one year after the Battle of Geonosis.

In a later discussion on TheForce.net's literature boards, statements were made by Kaufman denying that this was treated as a definitive figure for the total army.<ref name="Kaufman">{{JCFCite|url=posts/21642877|board=Literature|thread=Guide to the Grand Army (Insider #84)|user=Ryan_Kaufman|date=2005-09-20|archivedate=20201018053645}}</ref> Additionally, most stories made since ''Attack of the Clones'' have shown dozens of battles, during many of which the clones sustained massive losses, casting doubt on arguments that they represented a "small, elite, special operations force" compared with regular battle droids. ''[[The Cestus Deception]]'' states that a million clones have died, and this is only as of [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], at most a year after the Geonosis invasion.

Some fans point to the existence of [[Spaarti cloning cylinder|Spaarti]] clones, and the massive number of recruits as possible explanations for high troop figures. Recruitment was mentioned in ''[[The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War]]'' and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'', and non-clone forces were seen in ''[[Jedi Trial]]''. Along with recruiting, one notable Jedi General Rahm Kota had his own serving Militia, as he saw the clones as unfit for battle. Spaarti cloning technology did not become available to the Republic until eight months after the [[Battle of Muunilinst/Legends|Battle of Muunilinst]], however, and the entire need for the clone army arose from the fact that the Republic had no central military organization to organize and carry out a war against the Separatist forces.

From sources like ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter]]'' and "[[Nomad]]," and even through various ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' comics and the novels ''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]'' and ''Jedi Trial'', there are several instances before and after the Battle of Geonosis showing non-clone soldiers serving as the majority of forces in military conflicts and being actively recruited by various military organizations. The reliability and quality of mercenaries and bounty hunters would not be high, and having large numbers of non-clone troops available from the outset of the war would have eliminated the need for a clone army and ended/prevented the controversy over the [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]]. However, the sources that depict non-clone forces prior to Geonosis are all referring to small-scale conflicts and minor battles.

Additionally, the non-clone military forces in the [[Battle of Praesitlyn]] in ''Jedi Trial'' were largely non-Republic volunteer forces. The [[Sons and Daughters of Freedom]] volunteer group, which contained 50,000 infantry troops and thousands more serving as armored unit and starship crew members, had its number of active members reduced to fewer than 2,000 operatives by the end of the battle. Moreover, the non-clone [[Praesitlyn Defense Force]] is entirely wiped out by the droid invasion force, with its own commander stating that non-clones are far less capable at combating battle droids. Likewise, while the Republic force sent to Praesitlyn consisted of only 20,000 clones, as well as additional non-clones, the only non-clones described in the novel are members of the command staff, starship crews, or support personnel. When that force faced off against the Separatist force of over one million droids, the clones took extremely heavy casualties and would have lost the battle had it not been for two successful suicide missions undertaken by the commanding [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] against the Separatist leadership.

Most of the initial clones would go on to fight in the Battle of Geonosis, with 192,000 clone troopers deployed on the battlefield there,<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations 2005">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']], p. 88</ref> and an unknown number serving as crew aboard the twenty [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|''Acclamator''-class assault ships]] that landed troops on the surface and/or stayed up in space or the additional "thousands" of Republic ships descending upon the grounded Confederate fleet.<ref>[[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'' novelization]]</ref>

The ground troops suffered heavy casualties; reports on the ships arriving at the medical facilities stationed at [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] listed 12,000 in need of triage, 8,000 walking wounded, and 72,000 combat-fit troops (''[[Republic Commando: Hard Contact]]''). General Grievous personally killed "entire clone trooper companies" or at least 288 troopers plus officers according to ''[[Unknown Soldier: The Story of General Grievous]]''. The 100,000 missing troops in the Ord Mantell report indicates either the use of multiple bases, that 100,000 was considered an appropriate garrison force (since one was established after the destruction of the Geonosis foundries in ''Star Wars: Complete Locations''), or that the Grand Army suffered over 50% casualties in its first victory.

The [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Revised Core Rulebook|Revised Core Rulebook]] states that the Republic immediately ordered 1,000 more ''Acclamator''s, indicating an army of at least 16 million troops, though whether they were intended for use by clones or non-clones is still in contention. Additionally, Traviss's own ''Triple Zero'' states that (at least up to that point of the war) all ''Acclamator''s are fully crewed by clones; combined with the twenty ''Acclamator''s present at Geonosis, that would mean that around 720,000 clones (or 24% the entire fighting force of the Republic) were tied up as largely noncombatant ship crews.

''Labyrinth of Evil'' describes clones being an omnipresent force on Coruscant, acting as security and anti-terrorism forces. ''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]'' also states that clone troopers are "ubiquitous" on Coruscant and other worlds.

The [[Sector Governance Decree/Legends|Sector Governance Decree]], individual governors were assigned to every planet in the Republic with regiments for their "protection." ([[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Revenge of the Sith'' novel]]). These actions were occurring at a time when the Republic forces were stretched thin and to the point of being pushed out of system after system (''Revenge of the Sith'' novel) as well as conducting the lengthy [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]] (''Star Wars: Clone Wars'', ''Revenge of the Sith'').

It is not surprising that Lama Su stated that all clones take this long in ''Attack of the Clones'', as the Kaminoans were businesspeople, and they were known to boast that their advanced model clones were the same as the stock units, just renamed to encourage higher sales ([[The Pengalan Tradeoff|''The Clone Wars: The Pengalan Tradeoff'']]).

The largest figure given for the Grand Army, so far, was millions of clone [[Division/Legends|divisions]], which were undergoing intense combat evaluation at the start of the war. This information was stated in ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Attack of the Clones]]'' (written by [[Simon Beecroft]] and [[Curtis Saxton]]), a book dealing directly with the worlds presented in the film. It was later restated in [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']], which gathered information from the previous three ''Inside…'' books, as well as new pieces of information.

As to the disparity with the numbers of battle droids, the short story ''[[Odds]]'' suggested that the CIS only had hundreds of millions of battle droids, with the larger figures being chalked up to propaganda on the part of Palpatine. This directly contradicts the article ''The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War'', which stated that Grievous commanded several quintillion droids. Any Republic propaganda directed towards its own people would have had little impact on the enemy's supreme commander, who had actual access to his own troops. On the other hand, the numbers given in ''The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War'' are somehow flawed by the huge disparity between the number of its various mechanized war machines (battle droids, ''Vulture'' droids, tri-fighters, tank droids, ''Hailfire'' droids, etc.), said to be only in the billions, and the quintillions that Grievous commanded. Standard battle droids are produced much quicker and are more dispensable than droid vehicles, however, and the "quintillions of battle droids" could also include CIS droids not used in battle (such as [[OOM pilot battle droid/Legends|OOM pilot battle droids]]). Also, in ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'': "Ambush," Count Dooku told King [[Katuunko/Legends|Katuunko]], "Our droid armies outnumber the Republic clones 100 to one," which, if taken literally, would put the numbers of clones in the quadrillions. However, although in most (if not all) major ground battles seen in ''The Clone Wars'' series, the CIS outnumbers the Republic significantly, there is almost always a similar number of Republic and CIS capital ships pitted against each other, although this could be partly explained by the fact that the ''Munificent''-class ships (which are the main ships used by the CIS in the show) carried 15 times the number of troops as the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class]]. This still leaves a huge number of droid ships that are not seen in use against the Republic (which goes against the standard CIS tactic of overwhelming numbers).

''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]'' also noted that, because of millions of Separatist warships being locked up in battles with Republic fleets, only a few thousand frigates and destroyers could assault the galactic capital towards the end of the war, accompanied by dozens of battleships. The ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization states (from the out-of-universe perspective of the narrator) that the CIS had pursued the war to that point through sheer force of numbers, with its droids outnumbering the clones, and even implies that the Confederacy was winning at several points.

With the [[Dorling Kindersley]] line of books (which first mentioned specific droid numbers), being written from an out-of-universe perspective, high droid numbers would have been stated matter-of-factly, and any deception would have been noted (as it was with the mention of [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] trading places with its sister ships, in DK's ''Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections'').

Additionally, a battle droid is not directly equivalent to a clone trooper; standard [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]] were cheap, expendable units, often used for foot patrol in civilian areas. They were typically deployed for combat in massed units that lacked the initiative and versatility of real soldiers, relying instead on sheer numbers to overwhelm opposition, although elite droids like [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]] and [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] were both numerous and relatively intelligent. ''Odds'' also depicts extensive sabotage of droid production lines. According to the story, the weakened droids are significantly easier for the clones to destroy, although clones have been shown being gunned down with similar ease. However, it is doubtful that the Republic managed to sabotage ''all'' major droid foundries.

Additionally, from the [[501st Journal]], it seems even elite units held a negative view of relatively small odds:
{{Quote|When we arrived on Kashyyyk, things were just as bad as we'd feared. The droids had us outgunned, outmaneuvered, and out manned by a five to one margin.|Retired [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]]|<ref name="BF2" />}}
That only a few dozen ships were seen on-screen in the ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' cartoon bears little meaning, as many battles in ''Star Wars'' are often fleshed out in different sources. The same series also showed hundreds of ''Providence''-class carrier/destroyers in the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]].

Another possibility is that the troop numbers Lama Su mentioned could have referred to only those troopers being trained in [[Tipoca City/Legends|Tipoca City]], although this conflicts with Obi-Wan Kenobi's statements during the [[First Battle of Kamino|Battle of Kamino]]:
{{Quote|Kamino still has about a million or more clone troopers in various stages of preparation…|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Republic 50">[[Republic 50|''Republic'' 50]]</ref>}}
It is also possible that Lama Su did not intend the term "unit" to refer to an individual soldier. If a "unit" referred to a battalion of 576 troopers (as Lama Su spoke of later in Obi-Wan's visit), then 200,000 of these would render 115,200,000 clones and the 1,000,000 others spoken of as 576,000,000. This grand total of 691,200,000 would be far more suitable for the core of a galactic army. A "unit" being a 2,304-clone regiment, the largest military division classified as a unit instead of a formation, would amount to 2,764,800,000 clones. Furthermore, if a "unit" refers to a legion, the closest formation in size to a real-life British division of 15,000 men, the 1,200,000 units would have more than 18,000,000,000 clones, a truly "grand" army, suitable for defeating the huge numbers of droids under the Confederacy.

However, the number of clone soldiers which can be seen standing in each formation at the end of ''Attack of the Clones'' amounts to 624 (26 per column and 24 per row), showing a disparity with the numbers presented in the Guide to the Grand Army. If a unit indeed amounts to one battalion, this would mean that the grand total of clones was 1,728,000,000, considering the 3 million units that many sources state, and counting a unit as a battalion of 576 clones. This is reasonable since Lama Su referred to the clones with both "units" and "battalions," which could imply that both terms are merely ways of stating 576-man units/battalions. It seems logical that the Kaminoans would have their smallest available package of troops be made up of several hundred men. Since cloning was a 10-year process and (since the training and feeding would also have to be taken into account) an expensive one, it would make no sense that anyone would want to buy a couple of men and have to wait for 10 years when they could come by ten times as many droids for a fraction of the cost, with a wait of perhaps a week.

Furthermore, all planetary and judicial forces loyal to the Republic were folded into the Grand Army, allowing the Republic, which enjoyed a large population advantage over the CIS to make up for the number of battle droids with possibly hundreds of trillions of organic, non-clone soldiers in all-out combat. However, a statement by Chancellor Palpatine implied there was no conscription of civilians, due to potential political consequences.<ref name="RC:TZ" /> But this implication is contradicted in ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' by the following statement:
{{Quote|Conscription, however, was a necessary reality. Countless beings of every species became draftees into the Grand Army of the Republic.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="The New Essential Chronology" />}}
Thus is it is likely that the Grand Army was combination of clones, draftees, and troops from local planetary armies.

In addition, the Confederate battleship [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']] made at least fourteen attacks, of which at least two occurred against three-ship task forces. Assuming that the other twelve were assaults on single ships, which seems unlikely, and that the ships were ''Venator'' Star Destroyers, which would fit with their prominence in this era and the relative importance of the ''Malevolence'', there must have been at least 88,800 clone casualties in crews alone. If these vessels were fully loaded, the casualty count rises to 112,800, almost a tenth of the supposed number of combat-ready clones. As the chief concern over the ''Malevolence'' was its ability to destroy the ships without any indication of its nature<ref name="RM">{{TCW|Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence''}}</ref> and not the casualties, this would seem to indicate a much larger clone army than stated in certain sources.

In ''Attack of The Clones'', Count Dooku stated that there were too many clones for the droids to combat. This is supported by an estimate given that, at the beginning of the war, the casualty ratio for members of the CIS versus the GAR is 20 to 1. Since there are supposed to be around 3 million droids present at the battle, and approximately 200,000 clones, the clone army there would have, by that estimate, easily been able to handle the droid army.

However, Count Dooku made this comment in reply to Nute Gunray's suggestion to "send all available droids into battle." Dooku desired a long, difficult war. Dooku needed the war to facilitate his rise to power with Palpatine. In [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (video game)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' video game]], an order is given to destroy the Droid Core Ships, as "each one houses enough firepower to threaten an entire planet." A similar description is given through Obi-Wan's thoughts in the novelization of Episode II. The CIS forces had a fair chance of holding out against the Republic longer, which may have led to a shortage in troops later in the war.

One million planets were contested in the war, so with a million troopers per world, the army would need to be one trillion strong.
